rows.what the ink shows: The opening parenthesis survives. The following short word is crossed through heavily; its first and medial bodies merge with the cancellation, so the proposed ses is not independently recoverable.
A tall initial t-like stroke and its leftward return remain, but the rest of the word lies along a long horizontal cancellation. Separate e-r-m-e-s bodies cannot be distinguished.
The initial s has a short oblique rise and low rounded return, followed by low connected e-s strokes. There is no tall l ascender as required for les.
The inserted first word consists of low n-o-n bodies; after the gap, the next word has a low beginning, two successive tall l strokes, and a low e-s ending.

A low left e curve meets the upright t with a rightward crossbar; the diagonal cancellation closes the left curve into a dark triangular outline. The uncancelled et in E et F on this page has the same low e and tall terminal t.
The capital P stem and upper loop remain clear above the horizontal strike. Below the strike are a small rounded o body, a low u trough, and a short final r hook.
At the right edge, a long looped descending q is followed by a low joined u/e body. The crossing deletion line passes beneath this added word without concealing its upper outline.
A small initial rise and a taller crossed upright survive, but the long dark cancellation absorbs the intervening low letter bodies. The visible remnants do not separately establish s-u-i-t-e.
The first letter is an open rounded c with no tall l ascender or initial s bend; a low middle body leads into the curled final s. The final curl descends into the cancellation of the line below.

The right end preserves a dotted i and looped l, then the long low lead and paired tall strokes of suffit. Earlier words are crossed by two strong strokes and overlapping ink from the line above; the proposed extra est cannot be distinguished there.

The three-stroke summation sign, slanted lambda, lowered i, and terminal oval 0 remain distinct. The relation between the indexed lambda and 0 is a dense dark knot crossed by the cancellation, so its direction and lower bar cannot be separated.

The initial group preserves the large C curve, small e loop and tall l of Cela. The following ink has low joined bodies, a small raised point and tall terminal strokes, but cancellation obscures enough of the word to leave résulte unconfirmed.
A long initial descender and several terminal arcs remain, but the broad cancellation covers the central letters. These surviving pieces do not independently establish the full word parties.
The short group before §2 has a small rounded initial a and a low extended final stroke for u; there is no tall initial d ascender.

The underlined phrase has two word groups. The first has a p descender, crossed t strokes and an i dot; the second starts with an open c and ends in a crowded crossed group followed by dotted i and a low ending, supporting corrections rather than en italiques.
Below the deletion line are a small rounded body, a taller stem crossing the line, and a broad terminal curve with a hook. The line breaks the connections needed to establish de securely.

A narrow descending loop survives at the beginning of the group after tel, but the following low bodies merge into the thick cancellation. The visible remainder cannot distinguish the full proposed que.
Above the tensor sign is one short, isolated curved oblique stroke. It has neither the length nor a baseline foot of a numeral 1, and reads as a prime.
